basis: Neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disease; retinal degeneration with visual loss commonly develops over the course (>30%), although timing varies in juvenile CLN2.

decisions.ocular: involved: progressive retinal degeneration with visual loss is common over the CLN2 course (>30%); juvenile onset can delay ocular manifestations.

basis: Aggressive systemic mast-cell neoplasm with eosinophilia; hepatic infiltration can occur, but damaging hepatic involvement in >=30% of this subtype is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly or infiltration alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction; a >=30% frequency of damaging liver involvement is not established for this subtype.

basis: Glycosylation defect with defining enteropathy and brain disease (80-99%); thrombocytopenia 3/3 and frequent coagulopathy. Qualifying renal, hepatic and ocular involvement omitted by cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: thrombocytopenia in 3/3, anemia in 2/2 and frequent coagulation abnormalities establish common secondary blood and coagulation dysfunction.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: protein-losing enteropathy and prominent gastrointestinal dysfunction are defining manifestations; enteropathy is documented in 1/1 assessed.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment, seizures and ataxia form a defining neurologic component; nervous-system abnormalities occur in 80-99%.

basis: Autoinflammatory disease with defining recurrent peritonitis (94%); inflammatory pleuritis occurs in 47% and arthritis in 39%. Renal amyloidosis is a minority complication.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: recurrent inflammatory peritonitis is a major diagnostic manifestation, documented in 164/175 (~94%); this is serosal inflammation rather than abdominal pain alone.

basis: Craniosynostosis defines disease; strabismus 30-79%, conductive hearing loss 7/7, and Chiari/cerebellar abnormalities 30-79%. Dental abnormalities omitted by cap; optic atrophy <30%.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus causes ocular motor dysfunction in 30-79%. Proptosis reflects shallow bony orbits and does not independently establish primary eye disease.

basis: BLNK antibody deficiency; protein-losing enteropathy in 1/1 supports intestinal dysfunction, with limited sampling. Neutropenia in 1/2 lacks evidence of persistence; infections are separate diseases.

decisions.haematologic: none: neutropenia in 1/2 does not establish persistent intrinsic blood-cell dysfunction; transient infection-associated neutropenia is insufficient.
decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: protein-losing enteropathy in 1/1 documents intestinal loss of function beyond infection susceptibility; the tiny sample limits confidence.

basis: Retroperitoneal hemangiopericytoma belongs to the fibroblastic/SFT spectrum; no covered organ of origin is specified. Perivascular morphology does not establish vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hemangiopericytoma/SFT is a mesenchymal tumor with a perivascular growth pattern, not inherently a tumor of vessels; retroperitoneal location supplies no covered organ.

basis: Eosinophilic blood disorder with immune-mediated tissue injury; skin involvement ~50-60% and pulmonary ~30-40%. Gastrointestinal involvement ~30% omitted by cap; cardiac frequency varies.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none under cap: direct gastrointestinal infiltration affects roughly 30%; retain the more frequent skin and pulmonary involvement alongside the two defining mechanism axes.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: eosinophil-mediated inflammatory tissue injury defines HES and supplies the immune-mediated mechanism, alongside its defining blood-cell abnormality.

basis: Blepharophimosis and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Adducted thumbs occur in 30-79%, but fixed contracture or intrinsic skeletal damage is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: adducted thumbs occur in 30-79%, but posture alone does not establish joint, bone or muscle damage; fixed contractures or functional skeletal defects are not documented.

basis: Aortic disease and skeletal connective-tissue abnormalities define LDS4; permanent atrophic dermal striae occur in 24/70 (34%). Dural ectasia lacks demonstrated neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: striae in 24/70 (~34%) represent permanent dermal atrophy and connective-tissue damage, meeting the threshold; they are not transient discoloration.
